title: Reflexivity of natural-number equality
formal_statement: forall n : nat, n = n
informal_statement: Every natural number n is equal to itself.

steps.text: Let n be any natural number.
Both sides are the same number, so the equality follows by reflexivity.

title: Zero on the left of addition
formal_statement: forall n : nat, 0 + n = n
informal_statement: For every natural number n, adding n to zero gives n.

steps.text: Fix a natural number n.
By the definition of addition, 0 + n reduces to n. The two sides are therefore equal.

title: Addition with a successor on the left
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, S n + m = S (n + m)
informal_statement: For natural numbers n and m, the successor of n plus m equals the successor of n + m.

steps.text: Take arbitrary natural numbers n and m.
The recursive clause defining addition rewrites S n + m as S (n + m), which is exactly the right-hand side.

title: Adding from one gives a successor
formal_statement: forall n : nat, 1 + n = S n
informal_statement: For every natural number n, 1 + n is the successor of n.

steps.text: Let n be a natural number.
Since 1 is S 0, the definition of addition reduces 1 + n to S (0 + n), and then to S n. This proves the equality.

title: Simplifying a zero inside the right summand
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, n + (0 + m) = n + m
informal_statement: For all natural numbers n and m, n + (0 + m) = n + m.

steps.text: Fix n and m.
The inner expression 0 + m reduces to m by definition. Substituting this reduction leaves the same expression on both sides.

title: Simplifying a zero inside the left summand
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, (0 + n) + m = n + m
informal_statement: For all natural numbers n and m, (0 + n) + m = n + m.

steps.text: Choose arbitrary natural numbers n and m.
First reduce 0 + n to n. Both sides now read n + m, so they are equal.

title: Using an equality assumption directly
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, n = m -> n = m
informal_statement: If natural numbers n and m satisfy n = m, then n = m.

steps.text: Fix n and m, and assume that n = m.
The desired equality is precisely the assumption.

title: Reversing an equality
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, n = m -> m = n
informal_statement: If n and m are natural numbers and n = m, then m = n.

steps.text: Let n and m be natural numbers with n = m.
By symmetry, it is enough to show n = m, and that is our assumption.

title: Equality is preserved by successor
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, n = m -> S n = S m
informal_statement: Equal natural numbers have equal successors: n = m implies S n = S m.

steps.text: Take n and m and assume n = m.
It suffices to prove that the arguments of the two successor expressions are equal.
That remaining equality is exactly the hypothesis n = m.

title: Replacing the left argument of addition
formal_statement: forall n m p : nat, n = m -> n + p = m + p
informal_statement: For natural numbers n, m, and p, if n = m then n + p = m + p.

steps.text: Fix n, m, and p and suppose n = m.
Replace n by m in the left-hand side. Both sides become m + p.

title: Replacing the right argument of addition
formal_statement: forall n m p : nat, n = m -> p + n = p + m
informal_statement: For natural numbers n, m, and p, n = m implies p + n = p + m.

steps.text: Let n, m, and p be natural numbers with n = m.
Use the assumed equality to replace n by m under addition. The resulting two sums are identical.

title: Replacing repeated occurrences in reverse
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, n = m -> n + n = m + m
informal_statement: If natural numbers n and m are equal, then n + n = m + m.

steps.text: Fix n and m and assume n = m.
Read the assumption from right to left and replace both occurrences of m by n. The conclusion becomes n + n = n + n.

title: Swapping summands known to be equal
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, n = m -> n + m = m + n
informal_statement: If n and m are equal natural numbers, then n + m = m + n.

steps.text: Take n and m with n = m.
Replace n by m throughout the conclusion. Both sides then equal m + m.

title: Substitution followed by the zero clause
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, n = 0 -> n + m = m
informal_statement: For natural numbers n and m, if n = 0 then n + m = m.

steps.text: Fix n and m, and assume n is zero.
Substitute zero for n. The goal is now 0 + m = m.
The defining zero clause of addition reduces the left-hand side to m, proving the claim.

title: Substitution followed by the successor clause
formal_statement: forall n m p : nat, n = S m -> n + p = S (m + p)
informal_statement: For natural numbers n, m, and p, if n is the successor of m then n + p = S (m + p).

steps.text: Take n, m, and p, and suppose n = S m.
Replace n by S m in the desired equality.
By the successor clause of addition, S m + p reduces to S (m + p), as required.

title: Zero on the right of addition
formal_statement: forall n : nat, n + 0 = n
informal_statement: For every natural number n, n + 0 = n.

steps.text: Let n be arbitrary and proceed by induction on n.
steps.code:
intros n.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: For n = 0, the equality 0 + 0 = 0 follows by simplifying the definition of addition.
For the successor case, assume k + 0 = k. The goal S k + 0 = S k simplifies to S (k + 0) = S k. Replacing k + 0 by k using the induction hypothesis makes the sides identical.

title: Adding one on the right
formal_statement: forall n : nat, n + 1 = S n
informal_statement: For every natural number n, n + 1 is the successor of n.

steps.text: Fix n and use induction on it.
steps.code:
intros n.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: When n is zero, both 0 + 1 and S 0 reduce to 1.
Assume k + 1 = S k. For S k, simplifying leaves S (k + 1) = S (S k). Equality of the arguments suffices, and it is exactly the induction hypothesis.

title: Moving a successor out of the right summand
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, n + S m = S (n + m)
informal_statement: For all natural numbers n and m, n + S m = S (n + m).

steps.text: Fix n and m. Induct on n while keeping m fixed.
steps.code:
intros n m.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: At zero, both sides simplify to S m.
Assume k + S m = S (k + m). The successor goal simplifies to S (k + S m) = S (S (k + m)). Use the hypothesis from left to right inside the outer successor, obtaining identical sides.

title: Associativity of addition
formal_statement: forall a b c : nat, (a + b) + c = a + (b + c)
informal_statement: For all natural numbers a, b, and c, (a + b) + c = a + (b + c).

steps.text: Fix a, b, and c, and induct on a.
steps.code:
intros a b c.
induction a as [| k IH].

steps.text: If a = 0, both sides reduce to b + c.
Assume (k + b) + c = k + (b + c). For a = S k, the recursive definition reduces the goal to S ((k + b) + c) = S (k + (b + c)). Rewriting with the induction hypothesis proves this equality.

title: Removing two trailing zero additions
formal_statement: forall n : nat, (n + 0) + 0 = n
informal_statement: Adding zero twice on the right leaves any natural number n unchanged: (n + 0) + 0 = n.

steps.text: Take an arbitrary n and induct on n.
steps.code:
intros n.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: For zero, the left-hand side reduces to zero, so the claim holds.
Suppose (k + 0) + 0 = k. At S k, simplification gives S ((k + 0) + 0) = S k. Substitute the induction hypothesis inside the successor to finish.

title: Removing a zero from the first summand
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, (n + 0) + m = n + m
informal_statement: For natural numbers n and m, (n + 0) + m = n + m.

steps.text: Fix n and m and perform induction on n.
steps.code:
intros n m.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: The zero case simplifies to m = m.
Assume (k + 0) + m = k + m. Simplifying the successor case produces S ((k + 0) + m) = S (k + m). It suffices to equate the arguments, which is the induction hypothesis.

title: Commuting addition with one
formal_statement: forall n : nat, n + 1 = 1 + n
informal_statement: For every natural number n, n + 1 = 1 + n.

steps.text: Let n be a natural number and induct on it.
steps.code:
intros n.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: For n = 0, both sums reduce to 1.
Assume k + 1 = 1 + k. At S k, simplification gives S (k + 1) = S (S k). It suffices to prove k + 1 = S k. This is the hypothesis, since 1 + k reduces to S k.

title: Moving two successors out of the right summand
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, n + S (S m) = S (S (n + m))
informal_statement: For natural numbers n and m, n + S (S m) = S (S (n + m)).

steps.text: Fix n and m, and use induction on n.
steps.code:
intros n m.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: When n = 0, both sides reduce to S (S m).
Assume k + S (S m) = S (S (k + m)). In the successor case, simplify the addition and remove the common outer successor. The remaining equality is the induction hypothesis.

title: Two successive increments on the right
formal_statement: forall n : nat, (n + 1) + 1 = S (S n)
informal_statement: For every natural number n, adding one twice gives its second successor: (n + 1) + 1 = S (S n).

steps.text: Fix n and prove the statement by induction on n.
steps.code:
intros n.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: For zero, each side computes to 2.
Assume (k + 1) + 1 = S (S k). The successor case reduces to S ((k + 1) + 1) = S (S (S k)). Rewrite the inner sum with the hypothesis, after which both sides coincide.

title: An increment inside the first summand
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, (n + 1) + m = S (n + m)
informal_statement: For all natural numbers n and m, (n + 1) + m = S (n + m).

steps.text: Take n and m and induct on n with m fixed.
steps.code:
intros n m.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: At n = 0, both sides simplify to S m.
Suppose (k + 1) + m = S (k + m). Simplification at S k gives S ((k + 1) + m) = S (S (k + m)). Equality of the arguments is sufficient and follows directly from the induction hypothesis.

title: Moving a leading one across an outer summand
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, n + (1 + m) = 1 + (n + m)
informal_statement: For natural numbers n and m, n + (1 + m) = 1 + (n + m).

steps.text: Fix n and m and proceed by induction on n.
steps.code:
intros n m.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: The base case has S m on both sides after simplification.

Assume k + (1 + m) = 1 + (k + m). The successor case simplifies to S (k + S m) = S (S (k + m)). Equality of the arguments suffices. It follows from the hypothesis by reducing the additions whose first argument is 1.

title: Extending a right-zero equality along a prefix
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, m + 0 = m -> (n + m) + 0 = n + m
informal_statement: Let n and m be natural numbers. Assuming m + 0 = m, prove (n + m) + 0 = n + m.

steps.text: Fix n and m, retain the assumption m + 0 = m, and induct on n.
steps.code:
intros n m H.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: For n = 0, simplification leaves m + 0 = m, which is the given assumption.
Assume (k + m) + 0 = k + m. At S k the goal reduces to S ((k + m) + 0) = S (k + m). It suffices to show equality of the arguments, supplied by the induction hypothesis.

title: Extending a right-one equality along a prefix
formal_statement: forall n m : nat, m + 1 = S m -> (n + m) + 1 = S (n + m)
informal_statement: For natural numbers n and m, assume m + 1 = S m. Then (n + m) + 1 = S (n + m).

steps.text: Fix n and m and assume m + 1 = S m. Induct on n.
steps.code:
intros n m H.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: At zero, the goal reduces to the supplied equality m + 1 = S m.
Assume (k + m) + 1 = S (k + m). For S k, simplification gives S ((k + m) + 1) = S (S (k + m)). Rewriting the argument on the left with the induction hypothesis proves the goal.

title: Lifting a commuting pair beneath a common prefix
formal_statement: forall n m p : nat, m + p = p + m -> (n + m) + p = (n + p) + m
informal_statement: Let n, m, and p be natural numbers. If m + p = p + m, then (n + m) + p = (n + p) + m.

steps.text: Fix n, m, and p and assume m + p = p + m. Induct on n.
steps.code:
intros n m p H.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: For n = 0, the required equality simplifies to m + p = p + m, exactly the assumption.
Assume (k + m) + p = (k + p) + m. For S k the goal simplifies to S ((k + m) + p) = S ((k + p) + m). Replacing the left argument using the induction hypothesis makes the successors equal.

title: Reassociating a sum with an inner successor
formal_statement: forall n m p : nat, (n + S m) + p = S (n + (m + p))
informal_statement: For natural numbers n, m, and p, (n + S m) + p = S (n + (m + p)).

steps.text: Fix n, m, and p and induct on n.
steps.code:
intros n m p.
induction n as [| k IH].

steps.text: At zero, both sides simplify to S (m + p).

Assume (k + S m) + p = S (k + (m + p)). Simplifying the successor case gives S ((k + S m) + p) = S (S (k + (m + p))). Rewrite the inner expression with the induction hypothesis; the sides are now identical.
